topicName: Linting and Testing with Molecule and ansible-lint
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Linting and Testing with Molecule and ansible-lint"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ensuring the quality, consistency, and correctness of Ansible content is critical for reliable automation. This tutorial explores how to use ansible-lint for static code analysis and Molecule for automated, scenario-based infrastructure testing."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Installation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before starting, ensure you have Python and pip installed. You will need to install Ansible, ansible-lint, and Molecule along with a driver such as Docker to run containerized tests."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"pip install ansible ansible-lint molecule molecule-plugins[docker]"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Static Analysis with ansible-lint"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"ansible-lint checks your playbooks, roles, and collections for practices and behavior that could potentially be improved. It helps enforce coding standards and security best practices."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"ansible-lint site.yml"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use an .ansible-lint configuration file in your project root to exclude specific paths or disable rules that do not fit your workflow."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Setting Up Molecule for Role Testing"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Molecule aids in the development and testing of Ansible roles. Initialize Molecule within an existing role directory using the following command:"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"molecule init scenario --driver-name docker"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring molecule.yml"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"The molecule.yml file defines the testing lifecycle, platforms, and provisioner settings. Below is a sample configuration targeting a Docker container running Ubuntu."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"---
dependency:
  name: galaxy
driver:
  name: docker
platforms:
  - name: instance
    image: "ubuntu:22.04"
    pre_build_image: true
provisioner:
  name: ansible
verifier:
  name: ansible"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Executing the Molecule Lifecycle"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Molecule provides a sequence of commands known as the test lifecycle. You can run individual steps or execute the complete test matrix."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"molecule create: Provisions the test instances."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"molecule converge: Runs the Ansible role against the instances."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"molecule verify: Executes verification playbooks (typically using testinfra or Ansible assertions) to validate idempotence and state."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"molecule destroy: Cleans up and removes the test instances."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"molecule test"},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"By integrating ansible-lint and Molecule into your CI/CD pipelines, you can catch syntax errors, enforce style guidelines, and verify functional correctness across multiple operating systems before pushing code to production."}]
